statement: Gimbal lock is the loss of one degree of freedom in a multi-dimensional mechanism or coordinate system occurring at certain alignments of axes. In Euler angle representations of rotations in three dimensions, it occurs because the map from the 3-torus $\mathbb{T}^3$ to the rotation space $\mathrm{SO}(3) \cong \mathbb{RP}^3$ is not a local homeomorphism at every point, causing the rank (degrees of freedom) to drop below 3; for instance, in the X-Y-Z convention when $\beta = \pi/2$, the rotation matrix degenerates to $R = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 0 & 1 \\ \sin(\alpha+\gamma) & \cos(\alpha+\gamma) & 0 \\ -\cos(\alpha+\gamma) & \sin(\alpha+\gamma) & 0 \end{bmatrix}$, locking rotation to the single combined angle $\alpha + \gamma$ about the $Z$ axis.

symbols.meaning: 3-torus, the source space of Euler angles
space of rotations for three-dimensional rigid bodies
three-dimensional real projective space, homeomorphic to SO(3)

properties.property: For mechanisms or coordinate systems with three or fewer nested gimbals, gimbal lock inevitably occurs at some point
properties.why: topological constraints dictate that there is no covering map from the 3-torus to 3-dimensional real projective space

properties.property: At the locked orientation $\beta = \pi/2$, varying $\alpha$ and $\gamma$ produces identical rotational effects
properties.why: the rotation angle becomes $\alpha + \gamma$ while the rotation axis remains fixed in the $Z$ direction

properties.property: Continuous tracking of an arbitrary trajectory near or through gimbal lock requires arbitrarily fast or discontinuous gimbal motions
properties.why: the ratio of surrounding gimbal motion to platform rotation approaches infinity at the singular point

properties.property: Gimbal lock does not invalidate Euler angles as a coordinate system, but restricts their suitability for practical numerical tracking
properties.why: Euler angles remain a well-defined coordinate system despite losing local homeomorphism with SO(3) at singular points

assumptions.assumption: Orientation in 3D is parameterized using three Euler angles or three nested mechanical gimbals
assumptions.breaks_when: Orientation is represented with quaternions, rotation matrices, or a fourth redundant gimbal

assumptions.assumption: The intermediate rotation axis remains non-perpendicular to the outer and inner gimbal axes
assumptions.breaks_when: The intermediate angle reaches $\pm \pi/2$, causing the outer and inner axes to align collinearly

failure_modes.mode: Loss of a rotational degree of freedom
failure_modes.signature: Two rotational parameters collapse into a single sum (e.g. $\alpha + \gamma$), leaving rotations about the perpendicular axis unachievable
failure_modes.cause: Parallel alignment of two gimbal axes

failure_modes.signature: Gimbal or joint motors demand infinite velocity (or attempt to flip 180 degrees in zero time) or freeze the platform
failure_modes.cause: Mechanical limits on angular velocity and acceleration encountering the infinite kinematic velocity ratio near singular axes
